findings.title: StrEnum equality lets plain strings bypass Market enum validation
findings.description: `SOURCE_BAR_STAMPINGS` is a `frozenset` of `TimeMeaning` `StrEnum` members at `src/manta_trading_engine/core_model/markets.py:48-50`, and `TimeMeaning` is a `StrEnum` at `src/manta_trading_engine/core_model/timestamps.py:38-45`. In `Market.__post_init__`, the check at `src/manta_trading_engine/core_model/markets.py:94-98` uses set membership, so raw strings such as `"period_start"` compare and hash like the corresponding enum member and are accepted even though the field is typed `TimeMeaning` at line 84. The same runtime-type gap appears in `calendar_id_for` at lines 106-110 (`ref.session_mode == mode` accepts `"regular"`) and `require_adjustment_basis` at lines 115-117 (`basis not in self.adjustment_bases` accepts `"raw"`). This is inconsistent with the explicit `_require_instance` guards for `SessionCalendarRef` at lines 63-67, `continuity_kind` at lines 102-104, `session_calendars` at line 146, and `adjustment_bases` at line 165. The constructor test at `tests/core_model/test_markets.py:94-98` rejects `"regular"` for `SessionCalendarRef`, while `tests/core_model/test_markets.py:121-123` and `tests/core_model/test_markets.py:159-161` only cover enum-valued stampings, not raw string equivalents. Add explicit enum instance checks before membership/comparison and parametrized rejection tests for raw string equivalents of accepted enum values.

findings.title: Validation order leaks TypeError and can silently drop invalid bases
findings.description: `_normalize_bases` builds `items = frozenset(bases)` at `src/manta_trading_engine/core_model/markets.py:161` before validating elements at lines 164-165. Any unhashable invalid element therefore raises `TypeError` instead of the documented `InvalidMarketError`. Because `AdjustmentBasis` is a `StrEnum` at `src/manta_trading_engine/core_model/markets.py:32-36`, a raw string twin such as `"raw"` has the same equality/hash as `AdjustmentBasis.RAW`; in an iterable like `[AdjustmentBasis.RAW, "raw"]`, the duplicate can collapse to the enum member before validation, so the invalid `str` is silently dropped. The same hash-before-validation problem can raise `TypeError` in `Market.__post_init__` at line 94 and in `require_adjustment_basis` at line 117 for unhashable invalid values. The rejection table at `tests/core_model/test_markets.py:102-124` only covers hashable enum values and strings such as `"raw2"`, so it does not catch these cases. Materialize `tuple(bases)`, validate every element with `_require_instance`, then build the `frozenset`; add tests for mixed enum/string-twin bases and unhashable invalid inputs.

findings.title: Uniformity test duplicates the fixture inventory instead of enforcing it
findings.description: `ALL_INSTRUMENT_FIXTURES` is defined at `src/manta_trading_engine/core_model/fixtures/instruments.py:55-61`, and the task breakdown says it is intended for the later parametrized tests and that the uniformity test is parametrized over it at `project-documents/user/tasks/102-tasks.market-and-instrument-model.md:194,212`. The implementation instead imports the five instruments individually at `tests/core_model/test_market_uniformity.py:16-22` and hand-builds `UNIFORM_ROWS` at lines 36-42, with no assertion that the rows' instruments equal `ALL_INSTRUMENT_FIXTURES`. The tuple is only used for ID distinctness at `tests/core_model/test_instruments.py:208-210`. If another fixture instrument is added to `ALL_INSTRUMENT_FIXTURES`, the uniformity invariant that "one code path serves every market" can silently stop covering it. Derive the parametrization from `ALL_INSTRUMENT_FIXTURES` or add a set-equality guard between that tuple and the row instruments.

findings.title: Unused 60-second constant leaves width duplicated across the uniformity test
findings.description: `SIXTY_SECONDS_NS` at `tests/core_model/test_market_uniformity.py:34` is never used. The test separately hard-codes `BarSpec.time(60)` at line 56 and five `start_ns + 60s` expected-end literals at lines 37-41. That leaves a dead constant and scatters the single bar-width value across six places, contrary to DRY and the project convention "Never scatter comparison values across code"; changing the width requires multiple coordinated edits and can desynchronize input and expected outputs. If the expected values must remain hand-derived literals, remove the dead constant; otherwise use one named width constant to construct both the `BarSpec` and the expected ends.
